findings.statement: a thousand keys in the memtable cost the routed scan at least 3x
findings.detail: 55932103 entries/s routed against 16765364 with a thousand unsealed keys (routed vs routed+memtable: greater 3.336x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 9.6%/19.1%)); the fast path over partitions is lost for every entry once any unsealed key lies past the scan's start

findings.statement: four level-0 segments without a memtable scan within 1.5x of the undrained shape
findings.detail: 7174237 entries/s undrained (three segments and the memtable) against 20494950 with four segments and no memtable (undrained vs four-l0: less 0.350x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 25.5%/4.6%)); the level-0 count is the cost

findings.statement: the undrained shape scans at least 5x slower than routed
findings.detail: 55932103 entries/s routed against 7174237 undrained (routed vs undrained: greater 7.796x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 9.6%/25.5%)), EXT.39's 8.6x inside one process

notes: four arms interleaved, the same ordered load each rep, the store left in four shapes: routed (flush); routed plus a thousand keys in the memtable; four level-0 segments and no memtable (seal, no partitioning); undrained (three segments and the memtable). Then ordered scans from random starts; entries per second
predictions registered in scanmerge-plan.md before the run
